notes:
Checked main nav (top-level 'Outlet' item), footer, and on-page copy in English (site is natively English per prior-pass notes; no local-Finnish terms needed). Site has exactly one clearance-type PLP: /en-us/outlet, whose own copy reads 'Welcome to every design fan's treasury! In our Scandinavian design outlet, you'll find a frequently updated selection of discontinued items and last in-stock pieces at up to 50% off. Please note that the gems in our design clearance sale are available only while stocks last...' - this is permanent-markdown/outlet language (discontinued stock + last-in-stock, ongoing rolling selection, not a dated campaign), so it clearly qualifies as Clearance under the brief's Clearance-vs-Sale test. Separately checked the site's other discount surface, 'Design Deals' (nav 'Deals' -> /en-us/design-deals, also linked from footer as 'Design Deals'): every offer block on that page carries an explicit expiry date, e.g. 'The offer is valid on new orders until 20/22/30/31 September 2026 or while stocks last... cannot be combined with other promotions or discounts' - a genuine time-bound promotional campaign, correctly EXCLUDED per the Sale-vs-Clearance rule; not recorded as a row (no ambiguity - the dated-expiry language is unambiguous evidence of a temporary sale, not clearance). The bare path /deals 404s ('The page you are looking for can't be found') and falls back to a generic 'Popular right now' recommendation carousel - not a real PLP, excluded. The Outlet page itself shows product-type filter chips (Furniture/Lighting/Decor/Kitchenware/Storage/Tableware/Rugs/Bathroom/Outdoor/Lifestyle & Housekeeping/Bedroom/For Kids) but these are ordinary in-page facet filters on the single Outlet listing, not separate site-defined child pages, so no sub-structure was invented. Count verified via Playwright-rendered DOM text '667 products' directly above the product grid (site is a Vue SPA; SSR HTML has no count, and the catalog-products JSON API silently falls back to the whole-catalogue total 22917 for unrecognized uris like '/outlet', a known trap from the prior Home-Decor pass, so DOM text was used instead).

[POLICY UPDATE 2026-09-11] Removed 1 Outlet-classified row(s) per corrected policy: Outlet is not Clearance.
